description_full: Alarm.com Holdings, Inc. operates a platform for connected properties in North America and internationally. It operates in two segments, Alarm.com and Other. The company offers residential solutions, such as alarm transmission, smart signal, smart arming, and personal safety and awareness, as well as real-time alerts and always-on monitoring; video monitoring solutions, including video analytics, remote video monitoring, AI deterrence, video doorbell, intelligent integration, and cell connector; scenes, video analytics triggers, smart thermostat schedules, responsive savings, precision comfort, HVAC monitoring service, places feature, whole home water safety solution, and energy usage and solar monitoring solution. It also provides clean energy software and services SaaS platform; commercial grade video solutions, commercial video analytics, smarter access control, enterprise dashboard and multi-site management, connected fleet solution, energy savings, proactive protection for valuables and inventory, temperature monitoring, daily safeguard, and professionally supported and low cost of ownership solutions. In addition, the company offers OpenEye software comprising video surveillance as a service, cameras, recorders, and other peripherals designed for video applications; forensic video search, point-of sale system integration, customer site mapping, and large-scale camera deployments enterprise-level requirements; shooter detection systems; service provider portal, service dashboard, installation and support service provider solutions; and AI-powered enhancements to professional monitoring and false alarm reduction. Further, it provides business management services; sales, marketing, training services; and home builder program hardware and services. The company was founded in 2000 and is headquartered in Tysons, Virginia.

financial_summary: Alarm.com Holdings, Inc. is a mid-cap technology business with a $3.2B market cap on $1.0B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +6% over the past three years and +17% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 18% against a 9% cost of capital — a 9-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $137M in free cash flow — roughly 14 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.16× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage runs at 7.7×.
Shareholder yield is only 1.3%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 5.6% of the shares.

sect: Its 13% operating margin runs 6pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It earns less of the sector's profit than its revenue share would suggest (0.56x).
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+1.8% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 530 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 19% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the top of its 52-week range, 6% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 30% and a beta of 0.90, it moves roughly with the market.
About $24.7M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 32% in the 2020 crash and 44% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The stock trades only 3% below its DCF fair value of $66.88, a thin margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 23%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $56.00 to $82.77 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 52% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 4.3% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 4.0% (vs the 8% bar).
The 5 covering analysts target $65.00 on average, in line with the price.
The price implies 3.8% annual cash-flow growth, 4pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 18% clears the cost of capital of 9.3% by 9pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.37).
It converts 14% of revenue into free cash flow, or 10% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.16x.
ROE of 16% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.5x equity multiplier).
It spends 26.7% of revenue on R&D and 3.3% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $393.6M.
Working capital ties up about 128 days of sales, a drag on cash generation.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 6.3% over 3 years, 10.3% over 5 years and 17.1% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded 9.8% a year over five years.
Capex runs only 0.5x depreciation (1.6% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 21, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own 5.6%, meaningful skin in the game, and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insiders have only sold over the past year (12 sales, net $4.6M sold).
Shareholder yield is a modest 1.3% (1.3% in buybacks).
The share count has shrunk 0.5% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 2,058 employees, each generates about $491K of revenue, 1.3x the Technology median, and productivity has risen 17.1% a year.
That works out to $67K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $563K (1x revenue per employee).
